pinterest.title: Getting Married in Italy as an Australian: The Legal Steps in Order
pinterest.description: Getting married in Italy as an Australian takes two documents: an Atto Notorio from the Italian consulate for your state, and a Nulla Osta sworn in person at the Australian Embassy in Rome or the Consulate-General in Milan. A Certificate of No Impediment is not valid in Italy. What to prepare at home, what to sign in Italy, what happens at the town hall, and where your marriage stands once you are back in Australia.

pinterest.title: Atto Notorio and Nulla Osta: Italy Wedding Paperwork From Australia
pinterest.description: Getting married in Italy from Australia? Before you fly: your birth certificate and Single Status Certificate, an official Italian translation by a NAATI-certified translator, a Notary Public's notarisation, then DFAT apostilles. The Atto Notorio is signed at your state's Italian consulate with four unrelated witnesses. Both documents are valid for six months, so time them to your date.

pinterest.title: Getting Married in Italy: The Order of Steps Once You Arrive
pinterest.description: In Italy the order is fixed. Sign the Nulla Osta in Rome or Milan, have it legalised at a Prefettura with a revenue stamp (marca da bollo) from a tabaccaio, then lodge your Declaration of Intent at the comune. Some comuni want that declaration three days before the wedding, so allow a working week. Ask for an Apostille on your marriage certificate before you leave Italy.

slides: Getting married in Italy as an Australian? Most guides are written for British or American couples. This is the Australian version.
You need two documents: an Atto Notorio from the Italian consulate for your state, and a Nulla Osta sworn in person in Rome or Milan.
A Certificate of No Impediment will not work. The Australian Embassy says these are not valid for use in Italy.
Mind the six-month window. Both documents are valid for six months, so a date that moves late can mean signing again.
Before you leave Australia: certificates, NAATI Italian translations, notarisation, then DFAT apostilles. DFAT publishes no set turnaround, so start early.
In Italy the order is fixed: sign the Nulla Osta in Rome or Milan, legalise it at a Prefettura, then lodge your declaration at the comune.
Back home, you can't register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised. Bring the certificate home with an Apostille.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Getting married in Italy as an Australian comes down to two documents, two countries and a sequence that has to run in the right order.

At home: the Atto Notorio, signed at the Italian consulate for your state with four witnesses who are not related to either of you. In Rome or Milan: the Nulla Osta, which each Australian partner signs in person, by appointment. Then a Prefettura, then the comune.

Two things catch couples out. A Certificate of No Impediment is not valid in Italy, and both documents expire six months after signing.

Our full guide covers what to prepare before you fly, the order of steps once you land, civil, Catholic and symbolic ceremonies, and where your marriage stands once you are home. Link in bio.
